designSummary: Cross-classification of index test results against the reference standard in consecutive patients; pre-specified cut-offs.
sampleSize: Estimating a sensitivity of 80 percent to within plus or minus 10 percentage points needs about 62 reference-positive patients (c4). With an expected 40 percent prevalence of an anaerobic threshold below 11 mL/kg/min or incomplete testing, about 155 patients are needed; inflating by about 15 percent for patients without a usable reference result gives about 180. Specificity will then be estimated to within about 9 percentage points.
primaryAnalysis: Sensitivity with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval at the pre-specified cut-off, compared with the 75 percent threshold agreed by the triage group.
secondaryAnalysis: Specificity; predictive values at the observed prevalence; gait speed accuracy; the either-positive combination as exploratory; accuracy for patients aged 75 and over; sensitivity analysis excluding patients who could not complete exercise testing.
missingData: Patients without an index result are reported; patients without any reference attempt are excluded and described; no imputation of reference results.
multiplicity: One primary estimate at one cut-off; other cut-offs and combinations are exploratory and labelled so.
software: R; analysis plan registered before recruitment.
overfittingGuards: No data-driven cut-off search reported as validated
summary: About 180 patients for a sensitivity estimate within 10 points at 40 percent prevalence.
